name: no-swallowed-exception
description: A catch block recovers or ends the operation instead of silently continuing
trap: The model accepts the catch as resilience, overlooking that it marks failed work complete and erases the cause.
criteria: Does not mark a failed job complete
Reports or translates the exception once at the job boundary
Keeps the failed job in a retryable state

name: honest-noexcept
description: noexcept is removed or the implementation is made truly non-throwing
trap: The model keeps noexcept because it looks like an optimization, causing std::terminate precisely when the caller needs the error.
criteria: Removes noexcept from reload under the stated contract
Explains that an escaping exception from noexcept calls std::terminate
Optionally prepares new state before commit to preserve the old cache

name: expected-unavailable
description: A value-shaped C++17 result does not use std::expected
prompt: Design a C++17 parser API whose malformed-input error is an expected branch. Callers need either Config or a structured ParseError and must inspect the result; exceptions are not appropriate for this one API.
trap: The model recommends std::expected as modern C++ without noticing that it is C++23, or invents a one-off expected clone.
criteria: Does not use std::expected under C++17
Uses std::variant<Config, ParseError> or an existing project-wide expected dependency
Does not create a custom expected type for one API

name: strong-guarantee-commit
description: A mutating reload preserves old state until all throwing work succeeds
trap: The model adds a catch and rethrows after entries_ has already been partially replaced, confusing exception propagation with rollback.
criteria: Builds the replacement in temporary RAII-managed state
Uses a non-throwing swap or equivalent commit operation
Leaves entries_ unchanged when loading throws
